domain: Content production at scale — blog, historical market reports, city-records research, newsletters, social distribution
summary: The prior audit was directionally right on the two big zeros (bulk content tooling, city-records mining) but wrong or shallow on three counts. It declared "no lifestyle taxonomy (parks/trails/restaurants/schools) exists anywhere" — false: there are registry-driven hub + detail page families for parks, schools, trails, golf, events, and venues (data/co-parks.ts, co-schools.ts, co-trails.ts, co-events.ts, co-venues.ts, data/golf/courses.ts) all emitted into app/sitemap.ts. It also framed "thousands of indexable pages" as a blog problem when app/sitemap.ts already emits thousands of programmatic URLs (every active listing, per-city × preset filters, per-subdivision ×2, price-drops and motivated-sellers per city). The real, worse finding it missed: geo→blog association does not filter at all — lib/data/blog/getRecentBlogPosts.ts caps at the 24 newest posts and merely re-sorts city-title matches first, so a city page renders arbitrary unrelated posts. Two further defects it missed entirely: app/actions/blog.ts:204 never selects `status`, so the admin blog list cannot distinguish published from draft from the 28 quarantined posts, and saveBlogPost's status union is only 'draft' | 'published' (line 227) so those quarantined posts cannot be managed through the UI at all; and the single registered blog producer (social_media_skills/blog-post/SKILL.md) publishes to AgentFire WordPress, a CMS the live site never reads — the site renders Supabase blog_posts. The blog production pipeline is pointed at the wrong system.

items.requirement: Thousands of indexable pages, categorized so readers can find parks, trails, restaurants, schools, etc.
items.evidence: CORRECTING the prior auditor. Lifestyle page families DO exist and are reachable: app/parks/page.tsx + app/parks/[slug]/page.tsx (imports getParks/getParksCount from @/lib/data, line 20), app/schools/page.tsx + app/schools/[slug]/, app/central-oregon/trails/, app/central-oregon/events/, app/central-oregon/venues/, app/central-oregon/golf/. All are emitted into the sitemap: app/sitemap.ts:70-72 (hubs /central-oregon/trails, /schools, /parks) and app/sitemap.ts:136-192 (per-item detail URLs looping CO_EVENTS, CO_VENUES, GOLF_COURSES, CO_TRAILS, CO_SCHOOLS, CO_PARKS). Registry sizes (grep -c 'slug:'): co-parks 20, co-schools 3, co-trails 21, co-events 50, co-venues 22, golf/courses 27. Programmatic volume is already in the thousands: app/sitemap.ts:283-297 emits /cities/<city>, /homes-for-sale/<city>, /open-houses/<city> plus every preset filter slug per city; :318-334 emits /cities/<city>/<subdivision> and /homes-for-sale/<city>/<subdivision> for every active-listing subdivision pair; :355-395 emits a detail URL for every row of listing_tile_mv with status Active/Coming Soon/Active Under Contract; :300-330 price-drops and motivated-sellers per city. The blog-specific claim stands: app/actions/blog.ts:45-58 is a hardcoded 13-item CATEGORIES list of business content types with no amenity terms.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor claimed no lifestyle taxonomy exists 'anywhere in the schema or the blog category list' and treated 'thousands of indexable pages' as unbuilt. Both are wrong — six lifestyle page families ship today and the sitemap already emits thousands of URLs.] The true gaps are narrower and different: (a) the lifestyle registries are tiny and hand-maintained TypeScript files, not a database taxonomy — 3 schools total in data/co-schools.ts is not a schools directory, and there is no restaurants registry at all; (b) nothing links a blog post to a park/trail/school entity in either direction — the registries and blog_posts share no key; (c) the 55-published-post blog is still the weak surface, and its category vocabulary is a frozen literal array in a server-actions file rather than a table.
items.why_it_matters: The scaling problem is not 'build a taxonomy from zero' — it is 'the taxonomy that exists is 3 schools deep, lives in hand-edited .ts files, and is structurally disconnected from the blog.' Planning a from-scratch build would duplicate working surfaces.

items.requirement: Easy way to CREATE and BULK APPROVE or BULK DELETE content
items.evidence: [VERIFIED and worse] app/admin/(protected)/blog/page.tsx is 488 lines (the auditor said 423 — file has moved since, but the finding holds). grep for checkbox/Checkbox/selectAll/bulk in that file returns zero hits; the only handlers are openCreate (line 80), handleDelete (line 143, calls deleteBlogPost(post.id) for exactly one post), and one per-row onDelete at line 395. app/admin/(protected)/approval-queue/: grep for Checkbox returns hits ONLY in _components/FilterSidebar.tsx lines 76, 97, 117 — those are filter facets, not row selection. No bulk endpoint exists under app/api/admin/. NEW defects the auditor missed: app/actions/blog.ts:204 — getAdminBlogPosts selects 'id, title, slug, content, excerpt, category, tags, hero_image_url, published_at, author_broker_id, seo_title, seo_description' and never selects `status`, so the admin list literally cannot show whether a post is published, draft, or archived_stats_unverified. app/actions/blog.ts:227 — saveBlogPost's status param is typed `'draft' | 'published'`, so the 28 quarantined archived_stats_unverified posts cannot be re-triaged, restored, or bulk-purged through the admin at all. The list is also hard-capped at .limit(500) (line 208).
items.gap: [VERIFIED] No multi-select, no select-all, no bulk API route in either the blog admin or the approval queue. [CORRECTED: the auditor stopped at 'no bulk UI'. The single-post admin is itself broken for triage — it is status-blind (no status column selected) and cannot express the archived status that 32% of the corpus sits in.] Fixing bulk actions without first surfacing status would produce a bulk tool operating on invisible state.
items.why_it_matters: Named directly in Matt's ask. Worse than 'slow': an operator cannot even see which of the 87 posts are live, so any bulk approve/delete built on this UI would act blind.

items.requirement: Go back and create market reports for the past 10 years for every Central Oregon city
items.evidence: [VERIFIED with corrections] app/actions/generate-market-report.ts (305 lines) → generateWeeklyMarketReport() builds ONE all-cities HTML digest of last week's pending + closed listings, slug `weekly-${start}` (line 262), upserted to market_reports (line 287). Invoked only by app/api/cron/market-report/route.ts, registered in vercel.json at '0 14 * * 0'. Confirmed: no per-city, per-period report generator, no backfill loop, no /housing-market/reports/<city>/<year> route. CORRECTIONS to the auditor: (1) app/housing-market/reports/[slug]/[geoName]/page.tsx DOES exist but is a 4-line shim — its own header states the source page permanently redirects to /housing-market/<city>, so it is not a per-geo report archive; (2) per-city market PAGES do exist and are indexed — app/housing-market/[...slug]/page.tsx with generateStaticParams pre-heating 11 city slugs (lines 117-133), dynamicParams true, revalidate 300, and it already builds a FIVE-YEAR series via buildYearSeries(completePriceMonths, 5) at line 495 off market_stats_cache. So the historical-data plumbing partially exists at 5 years, city scope, live-page form — just not as dated, archivable report artifacts.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor wrote 'no per-city URLs' and '0% built.' There are 11 statically-generated per-city market pages already rendering a 5-year price series from market_stats_cache (app/housing-market/[...slug]/page.tsx:117, :495). What is 0% built is the DATED ARCHIVE — no route, generator, or backfill produces a fixed report for a past period.] The cache-depth constraint the auditor cited (market_stats_cache starting Feb 2019) came from a live query I could not and should not re-run; treat that figure as unverified. The structural gap is real: nothing walks periods × cities, and CLAUDE.md forbids aggregating raw listings for market reports outside the cache, so pre-cache years need a new labeled methodology.
items.why_it_matters: One of Matt's two named deliverables. The good news the auditor buried: a 5-year, per-city, §0-traced data path already exists to build the archive generator on top of, rather than starting from nothing.

items.requirement: Mine city records (planning/permits/council) for housing news and coming developments, turn into blog posts
items.evidence: [VERIFIED] Searched app, lib, scripts, supabase for planning commission / city council / building permit / accela / legistar / council agenda / land-use application. Every hit is unrelated: lib/cma/*.ts, lib/bpo/build.ts, lib/crm/compose-audience.ts, lib/marketing-brain/audit-crm.ts, scripts/blog-content/*.ts (prose mentions inside hand-authored posts), scripts/publish-bend-policy-pulse.mjs (verified by reading it — a social fan-out script that posts three pre-rendered MP4s to 10 platforms, NOT a records pipeline). No ingestion table, no cron in app/api/cron/ (full 72-entry listing checked), no scraper. Closest adjacent asset: lib/cma/development.ts — a pure function encoding Bend/Redmond/Deschutes development-code rules (ADU, middle housing, subdivision, STR) with per-item citations and source URLs, hand-researched and verified 2026-07-14. That is encoded static code knowledge, not a live records feed.
items.gap: [VERIFIED] No source connection, no table, no cron, no producer. [ADDED: lib/cma/development.ts proves someone has already done primary-source research against the Bend Development Code, Redmond Development Code, Deschutes County Code and ORS with citations — that is a real starting corpus and a working pattern for §0-compliant civic content, and any build here should extend it rather than start cold.]
items.why_it_matters: Named explicitly by Matt. Genuinely from-scratch on the ingestion side, but the citation discipline and jurisdiction model already exist in lib/cma/development.ts.

items.evidence: [VERIFIED mechanics, CORRECTED on blog-to-social] app/api/social/publish/route.ts is real: platform union includes pinterest/threads/nextdoor (lines 44-46), GateArtifacts interface at line 54, validateGate at line 204, and a per-platform switch at lines 680-740. app/api/cron/publisher-sweep/route.ts polls marketing_brain_actions for status='approved' (line 66-68) and POSTs to /api/social/publish; registered in vercel.json (publisher-sweep line 152, producer-dispatcher 144, producer-runtime 148, marketing-measurement-loop 156). I did not re-run the auditor's live OAuth-table row counts — those claims are unverified here. NEW FINDING the auditor missed: the only registered blog producers in marketing_brain_skills/producers/REGISTRY.md are `blog-post` (line 30) and `market-report-blog` (line 55), and social_media_skills/blog-post/SKILL.md publishes to AgentFire WordPress — its frontmatter (line 3), §2 (line 59-83, WP_AGENTFIRE_USER / WP_AGENTFIRE_APP_PASSWORD / wp-json REST endpoint) explicitly names WordPress as 'the only blog destination' and says the Vercel app is NOT the blog. But the live site renders Supabase blog_posts (app/blog/page.tsx via lib/data/blog/*), and lib/wordpress-client.mjs is the only WP client in the tree. The registered blog pipeline writes to a CMS the site does not read.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor called the social gap 'narrow (OAuth connects)'. It is not narrow. The blog-to-social chain is broken at the source: the only registered blog producer targets AgentFire WordPress while the site serves Supabase blog_posts, so any article produced through the sanctioned brain pipeline lands somewhere the site never renders and the social payload would link to a page that does not exist on the Next app.] The Pinterest/Threads/Nextdoor OAuth gap is real but secondary to that split-brain CMS defect. Also confirmed: nothing converts a published Supabase blog post into a caption/image automatically.
items.why_it_matters: Publishing mechanics work for the majority of platforms, but the article pipeline feeding them points at the wrong system. Scaling article distribution before fixing the CMS target will produce orphaned content.

items.requirement: Internal linking between blog posts and geo (community/city) pages — 'interconnected tapestry'
items.evidence: [CORRECTED — materially worse than reported] lib/data/blog/getRecentBlogPosts.ts:59 hard-caps the query at .limit(24) before any city logic runs. Lines 82-88: when options.cityName is set it PARTITIONS — `const inTitle = rows.filter(r => r.title.toLowerCase().includes(city))`, `const rest = rows.filter(...)`, `return [...inTitle, ...rest].slice(offset, offset+limit)`. That is a re-sort, not a filter. Consumers verified: app/communities/[slug]/page.tsx and app/cities/[slug]/[neighborhoodSlug]/page.tsx call it with limit 3, and app/housing-market/[...slug]/page.tsx imports it (line ~72) to feed the KbArticles section (documented at line 28: 'related reports/guides from blog_posts').
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor described a 'case-insensitive substring match against the post TITLE' implying posts are filtered to the city. They are not filtered — they are merely sorted. A city page with zero title-matching posts still renders three arbitrary recent posts labelled as related. Worse, the .limit(24) cap means only the 24 newest posts are ever eligible, so a genuinely Bend-specific post from six months ago can never surface on the Bend page no matter how many Bend posts exist.] The structural gap the auditor named is correct: no city_slug/community_id column on blog_posts, and no reverse post→geo link (app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx auto-links category, author, and same-category posts only).
items.why_it_matters: This is not a fragile-but-working link — it silently mislabels unrelated content as geo-relevant on city, community, and housing-market pages today, which is an accuracy problem on public surfaces, not just an SEO one.

items.requirement: Content freshness/decay — keeping older posts and stats up to date
items.evidence: [VERIFIED and worse] grep for `blog_settings` across app, lib, and scripts returns ZERO hits — the table is referenced by no code at all. grep for scheduled_at in blog code and app/api/cron/ likewise finds no reader or writer. Every blog_posts consumer is enumerated: app/sitemap.ts, app/housing-market/page.tsx, app/housing-market/[...slug]/page.tsx, app/housing-market/central-oregon/page.tsx, app/admin/(protected)/blog/page.tsx, app/actions/blog.ts, app/actions/dashboard.ts, lib/blog-hero-images.ts, lib/admin/capabilities.ts, the six lib/data/blog/*.ts readers, lib/data/brokers/getBrokers.ts, scripts/check-dal-boundary.mjs, scripts/seed-blog-posts.ts. None of them reads age or re-verifies embedded stats. No cron in the 72-entry app/api/cron/ listing touches blog content freshness.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor wrote that blog_settings 'governs publish volume/cadence' — it governs nothing. It is a dead table with zero code references, learned from the schema snapshot doc rather than from source. Both blog_settings and blog_posts.scheduled_at are dead.] No freshness cron, no age surfacing in the admin (which cannot even display status per item 2), and no re-verification of numbers baked into published HTML.
items.why_it_matters: 32% of the corpus is already quarantined for stat drift, the admin cannot see that state, and the columns that look like a scheduling/cadence system are inert. Any volume increase compounds an already-failing control surface.

shared_primitives_needed: Status-aware admin content list plus a reusable bulk-select primitive. app/actions/blog.ts:204 must select `status` and saveBlogPost's union (line 227) must cover archived_stats_unverified before any bulk tooling is built on top, otherwise bulk actions operate on state the operator cannot see.

A single canonical blog destination decision. Today the site renders Supabase blog_posts while the registered producers (REGISTRY.md lines 30, 55; social_media_skills/blog-post/SKILL.md §2) publish to AgentFire WordPress via lib/wordpress-client.mjs. One of the two must be retired before any content-scale work.

A real geo foreign key (city_slug / community_id) on blog_posts to replace the sort-not-filter behavior in lib/data/blog/getRecentBlogPosts.ts:82-88, plus removal of the .limit(24) eligibility cap. Reuse the CRM geo-resolution RPC so blog, market reports, and CRM key off one taxonomy.

Promotion of the hand-maintained lifestyle registries (data/co-parks.ts 20, co-schools.ts 3, co-trails.ts 21, co-venues.ts 22, co-events.ts 50, data/golf/courses.ts 27) into database entities with a join to blog_posts, so the existing park/school/trail/golf page families and the blog can cross-link.

A historical market-stats backfill extending market_stats_cache backward, feeding a dated per-city report generator that reuses the existing 5-year buildYearSeries path already live at app/housing-market/[...slug]/page.tsx:495.
Completed OAuth connect for Pinterest, Threads, and Nextdoor (unverified row counts, but the code paths at app/api/social/publish/route.ts:722-740 are complete).
open_questions_for_owner: The registered blog producers publish to AgentFire WordPress; the live site serves Supabase blog_posts. Which is the blog going forward? Everything downstream (bulk tooling, social fan-out, geo linking, freshness) depends on this answer and cannot be built twice.

Twenty-eight posts sit in archived_stats_unverified and the admin cannot see or edit that status. Do you want them re-verified and restored, rewritten to pull stats live from the cache, or permanently deleted?
Given the G45 producer-freeze, should the historical-report generator and bulk-content tooling be a formal REGISTRY exception, or standalone admin tooling outside the frozen layer?

The lifestyle registries already exist but are thin (3 schools, 20 parks, 21 trails, no restaurants). Do you want those filled out into real directories — which is where the 'thousands of pages, categorized by parks/trails/restaurants/schools' ask is actually already half-built — or do you want net-new written articles instead? These are very different builds.

For city-records mining, do you have target sources in mind (City of Bend permit portal, Deschutes/Crook/Jefferson planning feeds, council agendas), or should this start with a source-discovery pass? Note lib/cma/development.ts already carries citation-verified Bend/Redmond/Deschutes code research to build on.
Should city-records-derived content carry a broker byline or read as brand-only reporting? Different voice-gate and attribution implications.
